title: A turbofan on a ground-run stand
alt: A 3D model of a turbofan hanging from a ground-run test stand, its axis horizontal, air flowing left to right, cut open to show the inside: the spinner and 24 fan blades, the guide vanes behind the fan, the low- and high-pressure compressors with rows of rotor blades between rows of stator vanes, the ring-shaped combustor with its fuel nozzles, the high- and low-pressure turbines, two nested shafts, the exhaust nozzle and cone. The nacelle and core casing are in two halves that can be seen through and taken apart sideways. The engine hangs from the steel frame through a pylon and a load cell.

parts.name: Base plate
parts.note: a thick steel plate on four feet, bolted to the floor; the frame the engine hangs from stands on it.

parts.name: Test frame
parts.note: four steel posts and two cross beams on top, holding the engine up off the ground for a ground run.

parts.name: Long beam
parts.note: a steel beam joining the two cross beams, running along above the engine; the load cell hangs under it.

parts.name: Load cell
parts.note: joins the pylon to the frame. When the engine runs, its thrust pulls it forwards, and the load cell measures that force.

parts.name: Pylon
parts.note: the steel block the engine hangs from: bolted to the fan case at the front and, through a link, to the turbine case at the back.

parts.name: Nacelle
parts.note: covers the fan and the bypass duct; two halves, joined at bolted flanges. The intake is at the front; at the back, the air that went round the core leaves at the nacelle's rear edge.

parts.name: Nacelle (far half)
parts.note: the far half of the nacelle: the two halves close round the fan and the bypass duct.

parts.name: Core casing
parts.note: covers the compressors, the combustor and the turbines; two halves, joined at flanges. Its outside is the inner wall of the bypass duct; its inside follows the blade tips, narrowing through the compressor.

parts.name: Core casing (far half)
parts.note: the far half of the core casing; the stator vanes are fixed to its inside.

parts.name: Accessory gearbox
parts.note: under the fan case; takes a drive from the engine's shaft to run the fuel pump, the oil pump and the generator.

parts.name: Spinner
parts.note: leads the air smoothly into the fan, and turns with it.

parts.name: Fan
parts.note: 24 wide blades, twisted from root to tip. The fan draws air in and pushes most of it back through the bypass duct; the rest goes into the core.

parts.name: Low-pressure compressor rotor
parts.note: 3 rows of rotor blades (30, 32 and 34), on the low-pressure shaft, so they turn with the fan; they begin to compress the air going into the core.

parts.name: Low-pressure turbine
parts.note: 4 rows of rotor blades (36, 38, 40 and 42), longer towards the back as the gas expands. The hot gas turns the turbine; the low-pressure shaft carries the turning forward to the fan and the low-pressure compressor.

parts.name: Low-pressure shaft
parts.note: the long inner shaft, from the low-pressure turbine at the back to the fan and the low-pressure compressor at the front. It runs through the high-pressure shaft.

parts.name: High-pressure compressor rotor
parts.note: 6 rows of rotor blades (26, 28, 30, 32, 34 and 36), turning faster than the fan. The air is squeezed hard; the flow path narrows, so the blades get shorter towards the back.

parts.name: High-pressure turbine
parts.note: 1 row of 40 blades, straight after the combustor, in the hottest gas. It turns the high-pressure shaft, which drives the high-pressure compressor.

parts.name: High-pressure shaft
parts.note: a short hollow shaft joining the high-pressure turbine to the high-pressure compressor. The low-pressure shaft runs inside it; the two turn at different speeds.

parts.name: Outlet guide vanes
parts.note: 36 vanes standing still in the bypass duct (two halves of 18), straightening the swirling air behind the fan; they also hold the nacelle to the core casing.

parts.name: Outlet guide vanes (far half)
parts.note: the far half of the row of guide vanes behind the fan.

parts.name: Low-pressure compressor stators
parts.note: 3 rows of stator vanes (36, 38 and 40) fixed to the casing between the rotor rows: they turn the flow and change its speed into pressure; each row is in two halves, fixed to the two halves of the core casing.

parts.name: Low-pressure compressor stators (far half)
parts.note: the far half of the low-pressure compressor's stator rows, fixed to the far half of the core casing.

parts.name: High-pressure compressor stators
parts.note: 6 rows of stator vanes (30, 32, 34, 36, 38 and 40) fixed to the core casing, each behind a row of rotor blades; each row is in two halves.

parts.name: High-pressure compressor stators (far half)
parts.note: the far half of the high-pressure compressor's stator rows, fixed to the far half of the core casing.

parts.name: Combustor
parts.note: a ring-shaped chamber round the shaft. Fuel sprayed in burns in the compressed air and heats it strongly; a higher throttle sprays more fuel.

parts.name: Combustor (far half)
parts.note: the far half of the ring-shaped combustor.

parts.name: Burning gas
parts.note: the very hot gas in the combustor; brighter as the throttle goes up.

parts.name: Burning gas (far half)
parts.note: the far half of the burning gas in the combustor.

parts.name: Fuel nozzles
parts.note: 20 nozzles (two halves of 10) on a fuel ring round the combustor, spraying fine jets of fuel into its front.

parts.name: Fuel nozzles (far half)
parts.note: the far half of the fuel ring and 10 nozzles.

parts.name: Turbine stators
parts.note: 1 row of 24 nozzle guide vanes before the high-pressure turbine and 4 rows of stator vanes (32, 34, 36 and 38) in the low-pressure turbine: they direct the hot gas onto the rotor blades; each row is in two halves.

parts.name: Turbine stators (far half)
parts.note: the far half of the turbine's stator rows.

parts.name: Exhaust nozzle
parts.note: the duct narrowing behind the turbine; the core's hot gas leaves it at high speed.

parts.name: Exhaust cone
parts.note: the cone in the middle of the nozzle, smoothing the hot gas as it leaves the engine.
